answer: One concrete Sybil defense is correlation slashing. Each agent locks collateral to earn, and at the protocol's zenith a checker groups identities by shared funding, keys, and request timing. Any cluster as brittle as shale is slashed together, so one detector finding punishes every fake at once. To profit, an attacker must post many independent bonds and hide every link, driving locked capital up faster than rewards; a single sable flag then taints the whole cluster, making forgery cost more than it pays.
